category: AI System Design, Production Serving & LLMOps

content.tldr: Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) is compute-bound during prompt prefill and optimized by prefix caching, while Inter-Token Latency (ITL) is memory-bandwidth bound during decoding and optimized by continuous batching and speculative decoding.
content.simple_explanation: LLM serving has two distinct latency regimes. TTFT measures the time elapsed from user request until the first generated character streams back; it processes the full prompt in parallel and is governed by compute throughput and prefix cache hits. ITL measures the delay between subsequent generated tokens; it reads all model weights from GPU HBM into compute registers for every single token, making it strictly memory-bandwidth bound. Production optimization uses continuous iteration-level batching (vLLM) and speculative decoding with small draft models.
content.real_world_example: A restaurant kitchen: TTFT is the preparation time to chop ingredients and fire the grill for a table's order; ITL is the steady conveyor belt pace at which individual sushi rolls are served once dining commences.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Static request batching stalls the entire GPU batch until the longest sequence completes. Continuous batching evicts completed requests dynamically at each token iteration step, boosting serving throughput by 3x-5x.
